notes:
1. How to Study Important Personalities

For TNPSC, identify each personality through:

  • Field.
  • Major contribution.
  • Work or discovery.
  • Institution or movement.
  • Award or recognition.
  • Tamil Nadu connection, where relevant.

2. Creator, Patron and Revivalist

  • A creator produces an artistic or literary work.
  • A patron supports or commissions a work.
  • A revivalist helps restore or popularise an existing tradition.
  • An institution-builder creates organisations that sustain a field.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Patron ≠ Architect

Revivalist ≠ Inventor

Institution-builder ≠ Discoverer

3. Raja Raja Chola I

  • Raja Raja Chola I ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
  • He was one of the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty.
  • He commissioned the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur.
📌 Must-Memorise

Raja Raja I → Brihadisvara Temple → Thanjavur

4. Brihadisvara Temple

  • The Brihadisvara Temple was completed around 1010 CE.
  • It is dedicated to Shiva.
  • It is a major example of Chola-Dravidian temple architecture.

5. Great Living Chola Temples

  • Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur forms part of the UNESCO-listed Great Living Chola Temples.

6. Rajendra Chola I

  • Rajendra Chola I was the son and successor of Raja Raja I.
  • He founded Gangaikondacholapuram.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajendra Chola I → Gangaikondacholapuram

7. Gangaikondacholapuram Temple

  • The Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikondacholapuram is associated with Rajendra Chola I.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Thanjavur Brihadisvara → Raja Raja I

Gangaikondacholapuram → Rajendra I

8. Mahendravarman I

  • Mahendravarman I was an important Pallava ruler.
  • His reign is especially associated with early Pallava rock-cut architecture.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mahendravarman I → Rock-Cut Pallava Architecture

9. Mandagapattu Inscription

  • The Mandagapattu inscription is associated with Mahendravarman I.
  • It refers to a temple constructed without conventional materials such as brick, timber, metal and mortar.

10. Narasimhavarman I

  • Narasimhavarman I was a Pallava ruler.
  • His famous title was Mamalla.
📌 Must-Memorise

Narasimhavarman I → Mamalla

11. Mamallapuram

  • Mamallapuram is closely associated with Narasimhavarman I.
  • His period witnessed major development of monumental rock-cut art.

12. Mamallapuram Monuments

Important monuments include:

  • Pancha Rathas.
  • Cave temples.
  • Arjuna's Penance or Descent of the Ganges relief.

13. Pallava Architecture Trap

  • Mahendravarman I → Early rock-cut architecture.
  • Narasimhavarman I → Mamallapuram monumental phase.

14. Rajasimha Pallava

  • Rajasimha was also known as Narasimhavarman II.
  • He is strongly associated with Pallava structural-temple architecture.

15. Kailasanatha Temple

  • Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram is associated with Rajasimha Pallava.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajasimha → Kailasanatha Temple → Kanchipuram

16. Shore Temple

  • The Shore Temple at Mamallapuram belongs to the mature Pallava structural-temple phase.

  • Krishnadevaraya was a major ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire.
  • He belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

He patronised:

  • Literature.
  • Scholars.
  • Temple architecture.

18. Amuktamalyada

  • Krishnadevaraya authored Amuktamalyada in Telugu.
📌 Must-Memorise

Krishnadevaraya → Amuktamalyada

19. Ashtadiggajas

  • Krishnadevaraya's court is traditionally associated with eight celebrated Telugu poets called the Ashtadiggajas.

20. Akbar

  • Mughal emperor Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605.

He strongly patronised:

  • Architecture.
  • Painting.
  • Manuscript illustration.
  • Music.

21. Fatehpur Sikri

  • Fatehpur Sikri is one of the major architectural centres associated with Akbar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Akbar → Fatehpur Sikri

  • His imperial atelier employed both Persian and Indian artists.

23. Jahangir

Jahangir showed a strong personal interest in:

  • Painting.
  • Portraiture.
  • Plants.
  • Animals.
  • Natural history.

Mughal painting under Jahangir developed greater emphasis on:

  • Realism.
  • Portraiture.
  • Natural-history studies.

25. Ustad Mansur

  • Ustad Mansur was a celebrated painter at Jahangir's court.
  • He is especially famous for natural-history paintings.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ustad Mansur → Jahangir → Natural-History Painting

26. Shah Jahan

  • Shah Jahan is associated with the height of Mughal monumental architecture.

27. Taj Mahal

Shah Jahan → Patron

28. Shah Jahan's Major Structures

He is also associated with:

  • Red Fort, Delhi.
  • Jama Masjid, Delhi.

29. Raja Ravi Varma

  • Raja Ravi Varma lived from 1848 to 1906.
  • He was one of modern India's best-known painters.

30. Ravi Varma's Style

He combined:

  • European academic techniques.
  • Indian mythological and epic subjects.

31. Ravi Varma Press

  • Oleographs and lithographic reproductions helped circulate his paintings widely.
  • His images popularised visual representations of Hindu deities and epic characters.
📌 Must-Memorise

Raja Ravi Varma → Painting + Mythological Subjects + Print Reproduction

  • Abanindranath Tagore was a major modern Indian painter.
  • He became closely associated with the Bengal School of Art.

33. Bharat Mata

  • Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata became an important image of cultural nationalism.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bharat Mata Painting → Abanindranath Tagore

34. Bengal School

  • The Bengal School developed partly as a reaction against European academic dominance in colonial art education.

35. E.B. Havell

  • E.B. Havell was closely associated with the revivalist artistic environment surrounding the Bengal School.

36. Nandalal Bose

  • Nandalal Bose was a major modern Indian artist.
  • He became closely associated with Santiniketan.

37. Haripura Posters

  • Nandalal Bose created celebrated works for the Haripura Congress Session of 1938.
📌 Must-Memorise

Haripura Posters → Nandalal Bose

38. Constitution Artwork

  • Nandalal Bose and artists associated with Santiniketan contributed decorative artwork to the original handwritten Constitution of India.

39. Amrita Sher-Gil

  • Amrita Sher-Gil lived from 1913 to 1941.
  • She was an important pioneer of modern Indian painting.

40. Sher-Gil's Style

Her work combined:

  • European artistic training.
  • Indian subjects.
  • Rural and everyday-life themes.

41. M.F. Husain

  • M.F. Husain became one of India's best-known modern painters.
  • He was associated with the Progressive Artists' Group.

42. Progressive Artists' Group

  • The Progressive Artists' Group was established in Bombay in 1947.

43. Chola Bronzes

  • Chola bronzes are among India's greatest sculptural traditions.
  • They were products of highly skilled artistic workshops and temple patronage.

44. Nataraja

  • The bronze image of Shiva as Nataraja became an internationally recognised symbol of Chola art.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Chola Bronze → Shiva Nataraja

45. Tansen

  • Tansen was one of the most famous musicians associated with Akbar's court.
  • He occupies an important place in the development of Hindustani classical music.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tansen → Akbar

46. Amir Khusrau

  • Amir Khusrau lived from 1253 to 1325.

He was:

  • A poet.
  • A musician.
  • An Indo-Persian cultural figure.

47. Nizamuddin Auliya

  • Amir Khusrau was a disciple of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya.
📌 Must-Memorise

Amir Khusrau → Nizamuddin Auliya

48. Amir Khusrau's Cultural Importance

He is securely associated with:

  • Persian literature in India.
  • Hindavi expression.
  • Indo-Persian literary and musical culture.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Many specific musical inventions are popularly attributed to Amir Khusrau, but not all are securely established historically.

49. Carnatic Trinity

The Carnatic Trinity consists of:

  • Tyagaraja.
  • Muthuswami Dikshitar.
  • Syama Sastri.
📌 Must-Memorise

Carnatic Trinity → Tyagaraja + Dikshitar + Syama Sastri

50. Tyagaraja

  • Tyagaraja lived from 1767 to 1847.
  • He was one of the greatest Carnatic composers.
  • Many of his compositions are in Telugu.

51. Tyagaraja and Rama

  • Tyagaraja's devotional compositions are strongly associated with Rama.

52. Pancharatna Kritis

  • The Pancharatna Kritis are among Tyagaraja's most celebrated compositions.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tyagaraja → Rama Devotion + Pancharatna Kritis

53. Muthuswami Dikshitar

  • Muthuswami Dikshitar lived from 1775 to 1835.
  • Many of his compositions are in Sanskrit.

54. Dikshitar's Contribution

He is known for:

  • Complex compositions.
  • Temple references.
  • Raga scholarship.

55. Syama Sastri

  • Syama Sastri lived from 1762 to 1827.
  • He was the third member of the Carnatic Trinity.

56. Syama Sastri and Kamakshi

  • Many of Syama Sastri's compositions are devoted to Goddess Kamakshi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Syama Sastri → Kamakshi

57. Purandara Dasa

  • Purandara Dasa belonged broadly to the fifteenth-sixteenth centuries.
  • He helped systematise foundational methods of Carnatic music instruction.
📌 Must-Memorise

Purandara Dasa → Father of Carnatic Music

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Purandara Dasa ≠ Member of Carnatic Trinity

58. M.S. Subbulakshmi

  • M.S. Subbulakshmi lived from 1916 to 2004.
  • She was born in Madurai.
  • She became one of India's greatest Carnatic vocalists.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

M.S. Subbulakshmi → Madurai → Carnatic Vocalist

59. United Nations Performance

  • M.S. Subbulakshmi performed at the United Nations in 1966.

60. Bharat Ratna

  • She received the Bharat Ratna in 1998.
  • She became the first musician to receive India's highest civilian honour.
📌 Must-Memorise

M.S. Subbulakshmi → Bharat Ratna → 1998

61. Shanmukhavadivu

  • M.S. Subbulakshmi's mother, Madurai Shanmukhavadivu, was a veena musician.

62. Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar

  • Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar was a major Carnatic vocalist.
  • He is associated with shaping the modern Carnatic concert format.

63. Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer

  • Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer was an influential twentieth-century Carnatic vocalist and teacher.

64. M. Balamuralikrishna

Balamuralikrishna was known for:

  • Composition.
  • Musical innovation.

65. Lalgudi Jayaraman

  • Lalgudi Jayaraman was a celebrated Carnatic violinist and composer.

66. Bharatanatyam

  • Bharatanatyam is one of India's major classical dance traditions.

📌 Must-Memorise

Bharatanatyam → Tamil Nadu

67. Sadir Tradition

  • Bharatanatyam has historical connections with older temple and court performance traditions including Sadir.

  • Rukmini Devi Arundale lived from 1904 to 1986.
  • She played a major role in the twentieth-century revival and institutionalisation of Bharatanatyam.

  • Rukmini Devi founded Kalakshetra in Madras in 1936.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kalakshetra → Rukmini Devi → 1936

70. Importance of Kalakshetra

Kalakshetra became a major institution for:

  • Bharatanatyam.
  • Carnatic music.
  • Traditional arts.

71. Bharatanatyam Trap

  • Rukmini Devi did not invent Bharatanatyam.
  • She was an important revivalist and institution-builder.

72. T. Balasaraswati

  • T. Balasaraswati lived from 1918 to 1984.
  • She was one of the greatest Bharatanatyam performers of the twentieth century.

73. Abhinaya

  • Balasaraswati was especially celebrated for abhinaya or expressive interpretation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Balasaraswati → Bharatanatyam → Abhinaya

74. Rukmini Devi vs Balasaraswati

  • Rukmini Devi → Institutional revival and Kalakshetra.
  • Balasaraswati → Hereditary performance tradition and abhinaya excellence.

75. E. Krishna Iyer

  • E. Krishna Iyer played an important role in defending and promoting Bharatanatyam during its twentieth-century revival.

76. Birju Maharaj

  • Birju Maharaj was one of the most celebrated modern masters of Kathak.
📌 Must-Memorise

Birju Maharaj → Kathak

77. Kathakali

  • Kathakali is a classical dance-drama tradition of Kerala.

78. Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair

  • Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair became one of the important twentieth-century Kathakali performers.

79. Kerala Kalamandalam

  • Kerala Kalamandalam was founded through the efforts of Vallathol Narayana Menon and associates.
  • It became a major institution for Kathakali and other Kerala performing arts.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kerala Kalamandalam → Vallathol Narayana Menon

80. Kuchipudi

  • Kuchipudi is a classical dance tradition associated with Andhra Pradesh.

81. Siddhendra Yogi

  • Siddhendra Yogi is traditionally associated with the development of the Kuchipudi dance-drama tradition.

82. Odissi

  • Odissi is a classical dance form associated with Odisha.

83. Kelucharan Mohapatra

  • Kelucharan Mohapatra was one of the most important twentieth-century gurus in the revival and development of Odissi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kelucharan Mohapatra → Odissi

84. Manipuri

  • Manipuri is associated with Manipur.

85. Mohiniyattam

  • Mohiniyattam is associated with Kerala.

86. Sattriya

  • Sattriya developed in Assam from Vaishnavite monastic traditions.

87. Srimanta Sankardeva

  • Srimanta Sankardeva was central to the Assamese Vaishnavite cultural tradition from which Sattriya developed.
📌 Must-Memorise

Sankardeva → Assam → Sattriya Tradition

88. Ebrahim Alkazi

  • Ebrahim Alkazi was an important modern Indian theatre director.
  • He became closely associated with the National School of Drama.

89. National School of Drama

  • The National School of Drama became one of India's major institutions for theatre training.

90. Habib Tanvir

  • Habib Tanvir was an important theatre personality.

He blended:

  • Folk traditions.
  • Modern theatre.

91. Sankaradas Swamigal

  • Sankaradas Swamigal is regarded as one of the foundational personalities of modern Tamil theatre.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Sankaradas Swamigal → Tamil Theatre

92. Boys Company Tradition

  • Sankaradas Swamigal is associated with Tamil drama and the Boys Company stage tradition.

93. Pammal Sambandha Mudaliar

  • Pammal Sambandha Mudaliar was another important personality in the reform and modernisation of Tamil drama.

94. Dadasaheb Phalke

  • Dhundiraj Govind Phalke is popularly called the Father of Indian Cinema.
📌 Must-Memorise

Dadasaheb Phalke → Father of Indian Cinema

95. Raja Harishchandra

  • Raja Harishchandra was released in 1913.
  • It is generally regarded as India's first full-length indigenous silent feature film.
📌 Must-Memorise

Raja Harishchandra → 1913 → Dadasaheb Phalke

96. Dadasaheb Phalke Award

  • India's highest honour in cinema is named after Dadasaheb Phalke.

97. Satyajit Ray

  • Satyajit Ray lived from 1921 to 1992.

He was:

  • A filmmaker.
  • Writer.
  • Illustrator.

98. Pather Panchali

  • Pather Panchali was released in 1955.
  • It is the first film of Ray's Apu Trilogy.
📌 Must-Memorise

Satyajit Ray → Pather Panchali → 1955

99. Satyajit Ray's Recognition

Ray received:

  • Bharat Ratna in 1992.
  • Honorary Academy Award in 1992.

100. K. Balachander

  • K. Balachander was an important Tamil filmmaker.

His films became known for:

  • Social themes.
  • Strong characterisation.

101. Sivaji Ganesan

Sivaji Ganesan became famous for:

  • Stage background.
  • Powerful dramatic performances.

102. M.G. Ramachandran

  • M.G. Ramachandran was a major Tamil film personality who later became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.

103. Major Arts Institutions

  • Kalakshetra → Dance and music.
  • Kerala Kalamandalam → Kerala performing arts.
  • National School of Drama → Theatre.
  • Sangeet Natak Akademi → Performing arts.
  • Lalit Kala Akademi → Visual arts.

104. Aryabhata

  • Aryabhata was born in 476 CE.
  • He was a major mathematician and astronomer.
📌 Must-Memorise

Aryabhata → Aryabhatiya

105. Aryabhatiya

  • Aryabhatiya is Aryabhata's major work.

It deals with:

  • Mathematics.
  • Astronomy.

106. Aryabhata's Mathematics

Aryabhata made major contributions to:

  • Arithmetic.
  • Algebra.
  • Trigonometry.

107. Value of Pi

  • Aryabhata gave a remarkably accurate approximation of π.

108. Earth's Rotation

  • Aryabhata explained the apparent daily movement of celestial bodies through the rotation of the Earth.

109. Eclipses

He gave scientific explanations for:

  • Solar eclipses.
  • Lunar eclipses.
📌 Must-Memorise

Aryabhata → Astronomy + Earth's Rotation + Eclipses

110. Brahmagupta

  • Brahmagupta was born in 598 CE.
  • He was a mathematician and astronomer.

111. Brahmasphutasiddhanta

  • Brahmagupta's major work was Brahmasphutasiddhanta.
📌 Must-Memorise

Brahmagupta → Brahmasphutasiddhanta

112. Zero

  • Brahmagupta formulated systematic mathematical rules involving zero.

113. Positive and Negative Numbers

  • His work also contained rules involving positive and negative numbers.
📌 Must-Memorise

Brahmagupta → Zero + Negative Numbers

114. Bhaskara I

  • Bhaskara I was a seventh-century mathematician and astronomer.

He is known for:

  • Commentary on Aryabhata.
  • Trigonometric approximations.
  • Mathematical astronomy.

115. Bhaskara II

  • Bhaskara II, also known as Bhaskaracharya, was born in 1114 CE.

116. Siddhanta Shiromani

  • Bhaskara II's major work is Siddhanta Shiromani.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bhaskara II → Siddhanta Shiromani

117. Lilavati

  • Lilavati deals mainly with arithmetic and mathematical problems.

118. Bijaganita

  • Bijaganita deals with algebra.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Lilavati → Arithmetic

Bijaganita → Algebra

119. Madhava of Sangamagrama

  • Madhava lived approximately during the fourteenth-fifteenth centuries.
  • He was associated with Kerala.

120. Kerala School

  • Madhava was a leading figure of the Kerala School of Mathematics and Astronomy.
📌 Must-Memorise

Madhava → Kerala School

121. Infinite Series

Madhava is associated with infinite series for:

  • Pi.
  • Sine.
  • Cosine.
  • Arctangent.

122. Nilakantha Somayaji

  • Nilakantha Somayaji was an important Kerala mathematician and astronomer.

123. Tantrasangraha

  • Nilakantha's major work was Tantrasangraha.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nilakantha Somayaji → Tantrasangraha

124. Srinivasa Ramanujan

  • Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887 at Erode in Tamil Nadu.
  • He died on 26 April 1920.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Ramanujan → Erode → Mathematics

125. Ramanujan's Fields

His work contributed to:

  • Number theory.
  • Infinite series.
  • Continued fractions.
  • Partition theory.
  • Modular forms.

126. G.H. Hardy

  • Ramanujan's work attracted British mathematician G.H. Hardy.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ramanujan → G.H. Hardy

127. Cambridge

  • Ramanujan travelled to Cambridge in 1914.

128. Fellow of the Royal Society

  • Ramanujan was elected Fellow of the Royal Society in 1918.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ramanujan → FRS → 1918

129. Trinity College

  • Ramanujan also became a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge.

130. Hardy–Ramanujan Number

  • 1729 is popularly called the Hardy–Ramanujan number.

131. Why 1729?

1729 can be expressed as:

  • 1³ + 12³.
  • 9³ + 10³.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ramanujan → 1729

132. National Mathematics Day

  • National Mathematics Day is observed on 22 December, Ramanujan's birthday.
📌 Must-Memorise

22 December → National Mathematics Day

133. C.V. Raman

  • Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was born on 7 November 1888 at Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

C.V. Raman → Tiruchirappalli → Physics

134. Raman Effect

  • C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect in 1928.
📌 Must-Memorise

Raman Effect → 1928

135. Meaning of Raman Effect

  • The Raman Effect refers to a change in the frequency or wavelength of light when it is scattered by molecules.

136. Nobel Prize

  • C.V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
📌 Must-Memorise

C.V. Raman → Nobel Physics → 1930

137. National Science Day

  • National Science Day is observed on 28 February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

National Science Day → Raman Effect

Not the date of Raman's Nobel Prize

138. Raman Research Institute

  • C.V. Raman later founded the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru.

139. Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar

  • Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was born in 1910.
  • He was the nephew of C.V. Raman.

140. Chandrasekhar Limit

  • His most famous contribution is the Chandrasekhar Limit.
📌 Must-Memorise

Chandrasekhar Limit → White Dwarf Stars

141. Approximate Limit

  • The Chandrasekhar Limit is approximately 1.4 times the mass of the Sun.

142. Nobel Prize

  • Chandrasekhar shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics with William A. Fowler.

143. Meghnad Saha

  • Meghnad Saha was born in 1893.
  • He became an important astrophysicist.

144. Saha Ionization Equation

  • His greatest scientific contribution was the Saha Ionization Equation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Meghnad Saha → Saha Ionization Equation

145. Stellar Spectra

  • The equation helped explain ionisation in stellar atmospheres and the spectra of stars.

146. Satyendra Nath Bose

  • S.N. Bose was born in 1894.
  • He became a pioneering physicist.

147. Bose–Einstein Statistics

  • His work led to Bose–Einstein statistics.

148. Albert Einstein

  • Einstein recognised the significance of Bose's work and extended the theory.

149. Bosons

  • The class of particles called bosons is named after S.N. Bose.
📌 Must-Memorise

S.N. Bose → Bosons

150. Jagadish Chandra Bose

J.C. Bose lived from 1858 onward and worked in:

  • Physics.
  • Plant physiology.

151. J.C. Bose's Research

He conducted important research on:

  • Radio waves.
  • Microwave optics.
  • Plant responses.

152. Crescograph

  • The crescograph is associated with J.C. Bose.
  • It was used to measure plant growth and responses.
📌 Must-Memorise

J.C. Bose → Crescograph

153. Bose Institute

  • J.C. Bose founded Bose Institute in 1917.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

J.C. Bose → Crescograph / Plant Science

S.N. Bose → Bosons / Quantum Statistics

154. Prafulla Chandra Ray

  • P.C. Ray was born in 1861.
  • He was a major Indian chemist.

155. Bengal Chemicals

  • P.C. Ray established Bengal Chemical and Pharmaceutical Works.
📌 Must-Memorise

P.C. Ray → Bengal Chemicals

156. History of Hindu Chemistry

  • A History of Hindu Chemistry is associated with P.C. Ray.

157. Homi J. Bhabha

  • Homi Bhabha was born in 1909.
  • He became a leading nuclear physicist.
📌 Must-Memorise

Homi Bhabha → Father of India's Nuclear Programme

158. TIFR

  • Bhabha played the leading role in establishing the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in 1945.
📌 Must-Memorise

TIFR → Homi Bhabha → 1945

159. Atomic Energy Commission

  • Homi Bhabha became the first Chairman of India's Atomic Energy Commission.

160. BARC

  • The nuclear research centre at Trombay was later named Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in his honour.

161. Vikram Sarabhai

  • Vikram Sarabhai was born in 1919.
  • He is widely regarded as the Father of the Indian Space Programme.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vikram Sarabhai → Indian Space Programme

162. Physical Research Laboratory

  • Sarabhai played a central role in establishing the Physical Research Laboratory at Ahmedabad in 1947.

163. INCOSPAR

  • He played a leading role in establishing the Indian National Committee for Space Research.

164. ISRO

ISRO → 1969 → Vikram Sarabhai Context

168. U.R. Rao

  • Udupi Ramachandra Rao played a major role in the development of India's satellite programme.

169. Aryabhata Satellite

  • Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975.

India's First Satellite → Aryabhata → 1975

⚠️ TNPSC Trap
